title: The 10 Best Corded Circular Saws
subtitle: Wired saws ranked from live Amazon data — full power for the least money, no batteries.
intro: A corded circular saw plugs in and gives you full, unlimited power for as long as you're cutting — no battery to charge or run flat, and the lowest price for the most muscle. It's the right choice for a fixed shop, long rip cuts, and anyone who'd rather not buy into a battery platform. SKIL and DEWALT own this category; a couple of names here, the SKIL 5280 and the SKILSAW worm drive, are near-legendary. If you want to cut anywhere without a cord, see the cordless list instead.

changelog.note: Prices, ratings and review counts re-checked on every listing. Biggest price moves: the SKILSAW SPT77WML-01 rose from $161.10 to $205.99; the SKILSAW SPT67WL-01 dropped from $109 to $88.01; the GALAX PRO 11A dropped from $39.99 to $32.29. Prices were captured during Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days sale, so some may be temporarily lower.
All 10 picks kept. The DEWALT DWE575SB dropped from $149 to $124.99 and the SKILSAW SPT77WML-01 from $187.99 to $161.10.

products.name: DEWALT DWE575SB 7-1/4" Circular Saw (electric brake)
products.verdict: The best all-around corded saw. Highest rated here at 4.8 stars, with an electric brake that stops the blade fast, a 57° bevel, and a light 8.8 lb body. The SKIL below is cheaper, but this is the better tool.
products.best_for: The best all-round corded saw, with a blade brake for safety.
products.skip_if: You're on a budget; the SKIL 5280 is half the price.
pros: Electric brake stops the blade on trigger release
cons: Twice the price of the budget SKIL

products.name: SKIL 5280-01 15 Amp 7-1/4" Circular Saw
products.verdict: The value legend, and the highest-scoring corded saw on this list. 14,000 reviews at 4.7 stars, full 15-amp power, and a laser guide for around $70. The most saw per dollar you can buy.
products.best_for: The most saw per dollar: 15 amps and a laser guide for about $70.
products.skip_if: You want an electric blade brake.
pros: Most-reviewed saw here — 14,192 ratings at 4.7 stars
cons: Basic build vs the DEWALT and SKILSAW

products.name: SKILSAW SPT77WML-01 15 Amp 7-1/4" Worm Drive Saw
products.verdict: The pro's saw. A worm-drive gearbox puts more torque to the blade for wet lumber and long rips, and the magnesium body keeps it to a light-for-a-worm-drive 11.5 lb. Overkill for a bookshelf; perfect if you frame houses.
products.best_for: Framing and long rips in wet or thick lumber.
products.skip_if: You cut a few boards a year; it's heavy and the priciest here.
pros: Worm-drive torque powers through wet, thick stock
Light magnesium build with a Diablo blade included
cons: Heavier and longer than a sidewinder

products.name: Makita 5007F 7-1/4" Circular Saw
products.verdict: A pro-grade corded classic — smooth, fast (5,800 rpm), and built to last, with twin LED lights on the cut line. A favorite of tradespeople who don't want a worm drive.
products.best_for: Tradespeople who want a fast, smooth sidewinder with LED cut-line lights.
products.skip_if: You're shopping on price; the SKIL cuts similarly for less.
pros: Built-in LED lights on the blade line
cons: Pricier than the SKIL for similar cuts

products.name: SKILSAW SPT67WL-01 15 Amp 7-1/4" Sidewinder Saw
products.verdict: Worm-drive power in a lighter sidewinder body. The Dual-Field motor runs cooler under load and the 56° bevel is generous — a great middle ground between the budget SKIL and the full worm drive.
products.best_for: Long cuts where a cooler-running motor matters, without worm-drive weight.
products.skip_if: You want a brake or laser guide.
pros: Dual-Field motor stays cool on long cuts
4.8 stars, lighter than a worm drive
cons: Fewer reviews than the big sellers

products.name: Skil 5080-01 13 Amp 7-1/4" Circular Saw
products.verdict: The cheapest name-brand 7-1/4" saw here. A 13-amp motor is a touch less muscle than the 15-amp models, but for occasional cuts around the house it's hard to argue with $44 and 5,000+ reviews.
products.best_for: Occasional cuts around the house at the lowest price for a name-brand full-size saw.
products.skip_if: You cut dense lumber often; 13 amps is a step down.
cons: 13 amps vs 15 on the better saws

products.name: DEWALT DWE575 7-1/4" Lightweight Circular Saw
products.verdict: The DWE575SB without the electric brake, for a bit less. Same light 8.8 lb chassis, 15-amp motor, and 57° bevel — a great DEWALT corded saw if you don't need the brake.
products.best_for: The DEWALT build for less, if you can live without the brake.
products.skip_if: You want the blade to stop fast; get the DWE575SB.
cons: No electric brake (that's the SB model)

products.name: SKIL 5180-01 14 Amp 7-1/4" Circular Saw
products.verdict: SKIL's mid-tier corded saw — a 14-amp motor that splits the difference between the budget 5080 and the 15-amp 5280. A solid, no-drama pick under $60.
products.skip_if: You want a long review history or a laser guide.

products.name: DOVAMAN 5.8A 4-1/2" Compact Corded Circular Saw
products.verdict: A one-handed compact corded saw for plywood, paneling, and flooring. Light and easy in tight spaces, with a laser guide — just know a 4-1/2" blade won't cut through a 2x4 in one pass.
products.best_for: One-handed cuts in plywood, paneling and flooring.
products.skip_if: You cut 2x4s; the 4-1/2 in blade can't get through in one pass.

products.name: GALAX PRO 11A 7-1/4" Corded Circular Saw
products.verdict: The budget floor for a full-size corded saw. An 11-amp motor is modest, but you get a real 7-1/4" blade, bevel adjustment, and dust collection for around $32.
products.best_for: A full-size 7-1/4 in saw for about $32 for occasional jobs.
products.skip_if: You want brand-name power and support.
pros: Bevel adjust plus a dust port
cons: 11-amp motor is weaker than name-brand saws

avoid.name: Bigheimer 4" "Mini Circular Saw" / Cut-Off Tool
avoid.flag: A 4" angle grinder with a saw guard — cuts 5/8" deep
avoid.verdict: This isn't a circular saw — it's a 4-inch angle grinder with a saw guard bolted on. It cuts 5/8 of an inch deep and spins at grinder speed. Wrong, and genuinely unsafe, for the work a circular saw does.
reasons: It cuts only 5/8 inch (16 mm) deep. A real circular saw cuts about 2-1/2 inches — enough to crosscut a 2x4 in one pass. At 5/8", it can't cut through standard lumber at all.
It's a 4-inch angle grinder with a saw guard, spinning at 12,000 RPM. Real circular saws run around 5,000-5,800 RPM; a wood blade at grinder speed is a kickback and injury risk.
It isn't even corded. The listing now says it runs on DEWALT 20V batteries and ships tool-only, so there's no battery or charger in the box.
No-name "Bigheimer" brand, and it carries the lowest star rating in the category at 3.6.
If you want to cut metal or tile, buy a grinder. To cut wood, buy a real circular saw.

buyers_guide.a: A corded saw gives you full, sustained power for the lowest price and never needs a battery — ideal for a fixed shop, long rip cuts, or if you don't want to buy into a battery platform. The trade is the cord: you need an outlet and you're managing a cable.

buyers_guide.q: How many amps do I need?
buyers_guide.a: 15 amps is full power and what the best saws use. 13-14 amps is a small step down that's fine for occasional home use. Under about 11 amps you're into budget or compact territory that struggles with thick or wet lumber.

7-1/4 inch is the full-size standard and cuts through 2x lumber in a single pass. 4-1/2 inch compact saws are for plywood, trim, and flooring — handy and light, but they can't crosscut framing lumber.

A sidewinder (in-line) saw is lighter and cheaper — what most people should buy. A worm-drive saw gears the motor for more torque and a front-heavy balance pros like for rip cuts and wet lumber; heavier and pricier.
An electric brake stops the spinning blade in a second or two when you release the trigger. It's a real safety feature — one reason the DEWALT DWE575SB is our top corded pick.
